question: According to the ND CDL manual, which trailer in a doubles or triples combination is most likely to turn over due to the "crack-the-whip" effect?
choice_a: The last trailer in the combination
choice_b: The first trailer directly behind the tractor
choice_c: The converter dolly
choice_d: All trailers equally
explanation: The manual states doubles and triples are more likely to turn over because of the crack-the-whip effect, and the last trailer in a combination is most likely to turn over.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.1.2 — Beware of the Crack-the-Whip Effect

question: To prevent trailer rollover when pulling doubles or triples on curves, ramps, and corners, a driver should do what?
choice_a: Accelerate through the turn to maintain momentum
choice_b: Steer gently and go slowly
choice_c: Use only the trailer hand brake
choice_d: Keep both hands off the wheel
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to steer gently and go slowly around corners, ramps, and curves to prevent trailers from rolling over.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.1.1 — Prevent Trailer from Rolling Over

question: Why are doubles and triples more likely to turn over than other combination vehicles, per the manual?
choice_a: They have fewer axles than single trailers
choice_b: They always carry heavier loads
choice_c: Of the "crack-the-whip" effect
choice_d: They lack antilock brakes entirely
explanation: The manual explains that doubles and triples are more likely to turn over than other combination vehicles because of the crack-the-whip effect.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.1.2 — Beware of the Crack-the-Whip Effect

question: Compared to inspecting a single combination vehicle, what does the manual say about inspecting doubles and triples?
choice_a: Fewer parts need to be checked
choice_b: Inspection is identical and requires no extra steps
choice_c: Only the lead trailer needs inspection
choice_d: There are more critical parts to check, and all of them should be checked
explanation: The manual states there are more critical parts to check when pulling two or three trailers, and drivers should follow the procedures to check them all.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.1.3 — Inspect Completely

question: Why must drivers of doubles and triples allow more following distance than drivers of other commercial vehicles?
choice_a: Doubles and triples take up more space and cannot be turned or stopped as suddenly
choice_b: Doubles and triples have superior braking systems
choice_c: State law requires it only for triples
choice_d: Their tires wear out faster than other vehicles
explanation: The manual notes doubles and triples take up more space, are longer, and cannot be turned or stopped suddenly, so drivers should allow more following distance.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.1.5 — Manage Space

question: What makes driving doubles and triples in adverse conditions especially risky, according to the manual?
choice_a: They have no mirrors for lane changes
choice_b: Greater length and more dead axles pulled by the drive axles increase the chance of skids and loss of traction
choice_c: They are lighter than single trailers
choice_d: They cannot legally use tire chains
explanation: The manual explains that in adverse conditions, the greater length and additional dead axles pulled by the drive axles create more chance for skids and loss of traction.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.1.6 — Adverse Conditions

question: What should a driver keep in mind when parking a doubles or triples rig?
choice_a: Always park in the spot closest to the entrance
choice_b: Parking brakes should never be set on a doubles rig
choice_c: Avoid a spot that cannot be pulled straight through, to avoid a long, difficult escape
choice_d: Only the rear trailer needs to be chocked
explanation: The manual warns drivers to avoid parking in a spot they cannot pull straight through and to be aware of how parking lots are arranged.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.1.7 — Parking the Vehicle

question: Converter dollies built on or after what date are required to have antilock brakes, and how are they identified?
choice_a: January 1, 2000; a red lamp on the right side
choice_b: July 1, 2014; no visible indicator is required
choice_c: March 1, 1998; a green lamp on the rear
choice_d: March 1, 1998; a yellow lamp on the left side of the dolly
explanation: The manual states converter dollies built on or after March 1, 1998, are required to have antilock brakes and will have a yellow lamp on the left side of the dolly.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.1.8 — Antilock Braking Systems on Converter Dollies

question: What is a converter dolly, as defined in the ND CDL manual?
choice_a: A coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel used to couple a semitrailer to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination
choice_b: A hydraulic lift used to raise the tractor's fifth wheel
choice_c: A brake control valve mounted on the tractor dashboard
choice_d: A type of emergency air line connector
explanation: The manual defines a converter gear on a dolly as a coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel by which a semitrailer can be coupled to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.2.1 — Coupling Twin Trailers

question: When the second (rear) trailer does not have spring brakes, what procedure secures it before coupling?
choice_a: Chock the wheels only; no air connections are needed
choice_b: Drive the tractor close, connect the emergency line, charge the trailer air tank, then disconnect the emergency line to set the emergency brakes
choice_c: Leave the trailer air tank empty until coupling is complete
choice_d: Apply only the tractor's parking brake
explanation: The manual describes driving the tractor close to the trailer, connecting the emergency line, charging the trailer air tank, and disconnecting the emergency line to set the trailer emergency brakes if it lacks spring brakes.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.2.1 — Coupling Twin Trailers

question: For the safest handling on the road, how should semitrailers of different weights be arranged in a doubles combination?
choice_a: The lighter trailer should be closest to the tractor
choice_b: Weight distribution between the two trailers does not matter
choice_c: The more heavily loaded semitrailer should be in the first position behind the tractor
choice_d: Both trailers must be loaded to exactly the same weight
explanation: The manual states that for the safest handling, the more heavily loaded semitrailer should be in the first position behind the tractor, with the lighter trailer in the rear.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.2.1 — Coupling Twin Trailers

question: If there is any doubt about whether a trailer's brakes are set during coupling, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Proceed with coupling regardless
choice_b: Disconnect the air lines immediately
choice_c: Call for roadside assistance before continuing
choice_d: Chock the wheels
explanation: The manual advises chocking the wheels if there is any doubt about whether the trailer's brakes are set.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.2.1 — Coupling Twin Trailers

question: How does the manual say a driver should test the coupling of a semitrailer to the tractor or dolly?
choice_a: By pulling against the pin of the second semitrailer
choice_b: By visually inspecting from a distance only
choice_c: By sounding the horn twice
choice_d: By checking tire pressure at all axles
explanation: The manual lists testing the coupling by pulling against the pin of the second semitrailer as a step in the coupling procedure.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.2.1 — Coupling Twin Trailers

question: What should a driver look for when making a visual check of the coupling?
choice_a: The trailer's license plate is clean and visible
choice_b: No space between upper and lower fifth wheel, and locking jaws closed on the kingpin
choice_c: The mudflaps are properly attached
choice_d: The tractor's headlights are correctly aimed
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to make a visual check of the coupling, verifying no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel and that the locking jaws are closed on the kingpin.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.2.1 — Coupling Twin Trailers

question: After coupling the converter dolly to the second trailer, what should be done with the converter dolly air tank petcock and the second trailer's shut-off valves?
choice_a: Left open at all times
choice_b: Removed entirely from the system
choice_c: Closed
choice_d: Replaced with new valves before proceeding
explanation: The manual directs the driver to close the converter dolly air tank petcock and the shut-off valves at the rear of the second trailer after coupling.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.2.1 — Coupling Twin Trailers

question: After coupling, how does a driver confirm that air pressure has reached the rear of the second trailer?
choice_a: By listening to the engine idle
choice_b: By checking the side mirrors
choice_c: By pressing the trailer hand brake exactly once
choice_d: By charging the trailer brakes (pushing the air supply knob in) and checking for air by opening the emergency line shut-off at the rear
explanation: The manual states to charge the trailer brakes by pushing the air supply knob in, then check for air at the rear of the second trailer by opening the emergency line shut-off.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.2.1 — Coupling Twin Trailers

question: Before beginning to uncouple the rear trailer of a twin-trailer rig, how should the rig be positioned and what should be done first?
choice_a: Parked in a straight line on firm, level ground, with parking brakes applied
choice_b: Parked on a hill facing downward for easier release
choice_c: Positioned in a curve for easier access
choice_d: Left with the engine off and no brakes applied
explanation: The manual's uncoupling procedure begins with parking the rig in a straight line on firm level ground and applying the parking brakes so the rig won't move.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.2.2 — Uncoupling Twin Trailers

question: When uncoupling the rear trailer, under what condition should its wheels be chocked?
choice_a: Only if the trailer will be moved again the same day
choice_b: If the second trailer does not have spring brakes
choice_c: Chocking is never part of the uncoupling procedure
choice_d: Only during winter months
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to chock the wheels of the second trailer if it doesn't have spring brakes when uncoupling.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.2.2 — Uncoupling Twin Trailers

question: Why should a driver never unlock the pintle hook while the converter dolly is still under the rear trailer?
choice_a: It will damage the trailer tires
choice_b: It voids the vehicle's manufacturer warranty
choice_c: The dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury and making re-coupling difficult
choice_d: It triggers the antilock brake warning lamp
explanation: The manual warns that unlocking the pintle hook with the dolly still under the rear trailer may cause the dolly tow bar to fly up, causing injury and making re-coupling difficult.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.2.2 — Uncoupling Twin Trailers

question: What is the correct method for coupling a tractor and first semitrailer to the second and third trailers of a triples rig?
choice_a: Couple all three trailers to the tractor simultaneously
choice_b: Couple the last trailer to the tractor first, then work forward
choice_c: Skip the converter dolly and connect trailers directly to one another
choice_d: Couple the tractor to the first trailer, then move the converter dolly into position and couple the first trailer to the second trailer using the doubles coupling method
explanation: The manual describes coupling the tractor to the first trailer, then moving the converter dolly into position and coupling using the method already described for doubles.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.2.3 — Coupling and Uncoupling Triple Trailers

question: When uncoupling a triple-trailer rig, which trailer is uncoupled first?
choice_a: The third (last) trailer, by pulling the dolly out and unhitching it
choice_b: The first trailer directly behind the tractor
choice_c: The middle trailer
choice_d: All three trailers are uncoupled simultaneously
explanation: The manual directs uncoupling the third trailer first by pulling the dolly out, then unhitching it using the method for uncoupling doubles.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.2.3 — Coupling and Uncoupling Triple Trailers

question: During a coupling system inspection, where should the locking jaws be positioned relative to the kingpin?
choice_a: Around the head of the kingpin
choice_b: Around the shank, not the head, of the kingpin
choice_c: They should not make contact with the kingpin
choice_d: Anywhere along the kingpin is acceptable
explanation: The manual specifies checking that the locking jaws are around the shank, not the head, of the kingpin during a coupling system inspection.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.3.1 — Additional Checks (Coupling System Areas)

question: When inspecting the shut-off valves on a doubles or triples rig, what positions should the rear valves of the front trailer(s) and the rear valve of the last trailer be in, respectively?
choice_a: Both closed
choice_b: Both open
choice_c: Front trailer(s)' rear valves OPEN; last trailer's rear valve CLOSED
choice_d: Front trailer(s)' rear valves CLOSED; last trailer's rear valve OPEN
explanation: The manual specifies the rear shut-off valves of front trailers should be OPEN while the rear valve of the last trailer should be CLOSED.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.3.1 — Additional Checks (Double and Triple Trailers)

question: What should be checked about the landing gear during a doubles/triples inspection?
choice_a: It should be partially lowered at all times while driving
choice_b: Only its paint condition matters
choice_c: It should be removed before highway driving
choice_d: It should be fully raised, with no missing parts, and the crank handle in place and secured
explanation: The manual's inspection checklist calls for the landing gear to be fully raised with no missing or damaged parts and the crank handle in place and secured.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.3.1 — Additional Checks (Landing Gear)

topic: Checking Air Flow to All Trailers
question: How does a driver check that air flows all the way to the rear of a doubles or triples combination?
choice_a: Push in the red trailer air supply knob, then open the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer and listen for escaping air
choice_b: Rev the engine to maximum RPM and observe the tachometer
choice_c: Check tire pressure at each axle with a gauge
choice_d: Turn off the parking brake without performing any other checks
explanation: The manual describes pushing in the red trailer air supply knob, going to the rear of the rig, and opening the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer to hear air escaping, confirming the system is charged.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.4.1 — Additional Airbrake Checks

question: When testing the tractor protection valve on a doubles/triples rig, within what air pressure range does the trailer air supply control usually pop out to the emergency position?
choice_a: 60 to 90 psi
choice_b: 20 to 45 psi
choice_c: 5 to 10 psi
choice_d: 100 to 120 psi
explanation: The manual states the trailer air supply control usually pops out to the emergency position within the range of 20 to 45 psi.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.4.1 — Additional Airbrake Checks

question: How should a driver test the trailer service brakes on a doubles/triples combination?
choice_a: By disconnecting the emergency line and observing the gauge
choice_b: By removing the wheel chocks and coasting downhill
choice_c: By checking for normal air pressure, releasing parking brakes, moving forward slowly, and applying the trailer brakes with the hand control (trolley valve)
choice_d: By shutting off the engine and coasting to a stop
explanation: The manual describes testing trailer service brakes by checking for normal air pressure, releasing the parking brakes, moving the vehicle forward slowly, and applying the trailer brakes with the hand control to feel them engage.
source_note: North Dakota CDL Manual (2025-2027), Section 7.4.1 — Additional Airbrake Checks
